Title: An algorithm for solving the Independent Set problem
Let G=(V,E) be a graph  on n=│V│ vertices and m=│E│  edges, an independent set is a subset
of its vertices that are pairwise not adjacent.The Independent Set problem [1] asks: given a graph
G and an integer k, does G have an independent set of size at least k?
In this note, an algorithm based on some remarks from Linear Algebra is proposed for solving this
problem.
First, we will prove two usefull lemmas, before establishing the main result of the
present note.
Let n be an integer>1 and for k such 1≤k<n let SUT(k) denote the set of nxn integer
matrices that are strictly upper triangular and such :
T∈ SUT(k) then :
Tj=t(0 ,…,0) for j such 1≤j ≤k
Tj≠t(0 ,…,0) for j such  k+1≤j ≤n
Tj-1,j=1 for j such  k+1≤j ≤n
where Tj is the j-th column of matrix T=(Ti,j )
For k=n let SUT(n)={θ}  where θ is the nxn null matrix.
Lemma 1 : if T∈ SUT(k) then Tp ∈ SUT(k+p-1)
Lemma 2 : for any  integer k such 1≤k≤n,
if T∈ SUT(k) then Tn-k+1=θ
(ii)
for any  integer h such 1≤h<k, if T∈ SUT(h) then Tn-k+1≠θ
Proof :
Since T∈ SUT(k) then Tn-k+1∈ SUT(n-k+1+k-1) by lemma 1.
Then Tn-k+1∈ SUT(n) ={θ}, then Tn-k+1=θ.
(ii)
Since T∈ SUT(h) then Tn-k+1∈ SUT(n-k+1+h-1) by lemma 1.
Then Tn-k+1∈ SUT(n-k+h). Since h<k then n-k+h<n and Tn-k+1≠θ.
CLAIM 1 : Given an integer k≤n and a graph G on n vertices, let A denote its
adjacency matrix, and UA the strictly upper triangular matrix extracted from A.
Then G  contains a maximum independent set of size k if and only if (UA)n-k+1=θ.

Suppose by induction that if G  contains a maximum independent set of size k<n

If we delete all incident edges of a non isolated vertex j of G, then G  contains a

Thus, the induction is proved.

size k then (UA)n-k+1≠θ :
if G does’nt contains a maximum independent set of size k then G contains a

Then

Since T∈ SUT(h) and h<k then Tn-k+1≠θ by lemma 2 (ii)
Then (UA) n-k+1≠θ .

CLAIM 2 : The Independent Set problem can be solved by an O(n4) time algorithm.
Proof :
Considere the following algorithm :
INPUT An integer k and the adjacency matrix A of a given graph G with n vertices
1 T←I
2  For j=1 to n-k+1 do T←TUA
3   If T=θ then OUTPUT « G contains a maximum independent set of size k »
Else OUTPUT « G does’nt contains a maximum independent set of size k »
The correctness of this algorithm is proved by claim 1’ proof.
Since the (non optimal)  computation of the multiplication of two matrices requires
O(n3) times, then the loop 2 and the complexity of this algorithm is O(n4).
